issues.what: The Use button is a very faint ring with grey text at low opacity. Over the neon arcade signs, vending machines and pedestrians (frames 015-032) it all but disappears, and the 'U' is cut off where it overlaps a sign. It never changes state, so the player cannot tell whether anything is in range to use.
issues.where: Bottom-right Use button, about 82px CSS across at (745-828, 285-367); worst in frames 015, 018, 021, 027, 030
issues.fix: Give it a solid dark backing (about 70% opacity) with a light border and white label. Keep it dim when nothing is in range, then light it up and replace 'Use' with the action, e.g. 'Serve' or 'Sit', when a target is in reach. Make it at least 64px across with a 12px margin to the edge.

issues.what: There is no movement control on screen at all. Nothing marks a joystick or a drag-to-look zone, so the left thumb has no target and a first-time player cannot tell how to climb the stairs.
issues.where: Left half of the screen, bottom-left thumb zone, in every frame
issues.fix: Show a ghost joystick ring at the bottom left (about 110px CSS) that follows the touch point, and add a one-time 'drag to look' hint on the right half.

issues.what: The pause and phone buttons are about 42x42 CSS px with only about 6px between them. That is under the 44pt minimum, and the gap invites mis-taps that open the phone when the player meant to pause, or the other way round.
issues.where: Top-right icon buttons at (742-783) and (790-831), y 11-52
issues.fix: Make them 48x48 with a 12px gap, or move the phone into a single menu button. Pause should not sit right next to a second primary action.

issues.what: The weather pill ('Steady rain 4.5 mm/h') has the same rounded, bordered button styling as the tappable icons beside it, but it looks informational. Its '4.5 mm/h' second line is about 11px CSS, grey, monospace and low contrast against the navy.
issues.fix: Remove the button border so it reads as a label, or make it obviously tappable. Drop the second line to its own icon plus number at 13px or larger in near-white, or remove it, since mm/h means little to players.

issues.what: The chapter banner stays on screen all the time, taking about 470x35 CSS px of the top-centre, which is the exact band where the bridge skyline and the terrace destination sit. Its text is about 12px and the progress string '¥100,000 · 40/30' is cryptic: 40/30 is over the goal but shows no check mark, and the money half gives no target in context.
issues.where: Top-centre objective banner, y 64-99, every frame
issues.fix: Show the banner for about 4 seconds after a change, then shrink it to a small chip ('Ch.3 · ¥100k/160k · ✓ roast'). Use two clear progress items with check marks, and move it to the left below the resources so the centre view stays open.

issues.what: The resource pill has no labels. The leaf '60', '61/100 L' and lightning '0.0/2.0' never explain what they measure, and 0.0/2.0 looks like a broken or empty meter. The numbers are readable (about 13px) but meaningless at a glance.
issues.fix: Use short labels or small fill bars for capped values (water, energy), and support tap-and-hold for a tooltip. Turn a value amber or red only when it needs attention.

issues.what: The HUD sits about 12px from the left and right edges. On an 844x390 landscape iPhone, the notch and rounded corners cover about 47px on one side and the home indicator covers the bottom, so the yen value or the pause button will be clipped and the Use button sits in the home-gesture zone.
issues.where: Edges of the screen: top-left resource pill, top-right buttons, bottom-right Use button
issues.fix: Apply env(safe-area-inset-left/right/bottom) padding to every HUD anchor, and keep the Use button at least 20px above the bottom inset.

issues.what: The payoff, a tea terrace with seated customers, cannot be read at phone size. The tables and stools are about 25px CSS tall, sit at the far end of the bridge right next to the crosshair dot, and show no visible seated customers. The scene reads as empty furniture. Meanwhile the street-level shop and pedestrians in the lower right are far brighter and pull the eye away.
issues.where: Centre of frames 015-032, terrace at about (385-440, 225-260); the lit shopfront at the lower right draws attention instead
issues.fix: Light the terrace warmly (lanterns, a bright awning) so it is the brightest thing on the bridge. Place customers facing the camera with strong colour silhouettes, and dim the ground-level shopfront. Consider moving the terrace closer to the stair top so it fills at least about 15% of the screen when you arrive.

issues.what: The bridge deck and its railing are almost the same flat navy, and the solid railing panels fill the lower-left third of the screen. Dense full-screen rain streaks add white noise on top. On a small screen the walkable path is hard to see and the eye has nowhere to rest.
issues.where: Lower-left half of frames 009-032 (railing and deck); rain covers everything
issues.fix: Lighten or texture the deck (wet reflections, tiles, a lit strip along the edge), and drop the railing to a lower, see-through balustrade. Cut rain streak density and opacity by about 40% on small viewports.

issues.what: The stairwell climb is close to black. Frames 003-012 are dark navy on navy with almost no step edges, and the RGB stripe decoration on the stair stringer is the most saturated thing in view, which pulls attention to a meaningless detail. The walk ends (033-034) facing a black wall with no cue about where to go.
issues.fix: Add nosing highlights or strip lights to the step edges and an overhead light at the landing. Tone down the RGB stripe. Point the player toward the terrace with a light or sound at the top.

issues.what: The crosshair is a 5px grey dot fixed at the centre. On touch it serves no purpose and is invisible against bright signs, yet it suggests a precision-aiming interaction that phones cannot support.
issues.where: Centre of the screen, every frame
issues.fix: Hide it on touch, or replace it with a reticle that only appears and snaps when an interactable is in range, paired with the contextual Use label.

issues.what: Clipped brown voxel blobs sit along the bottom edge (likely held items or hands) and read as rendering artefacts. They sit exactly where a thumb would rest.
issues.where: Bottom edge, about x 210-260 and 590-650 CSS; frames 000, 012, 033, 034
issues.fix: Either show the held item fully and deliberately in a corner that thumbs do not cover, or hide it on mobile.

verdict: The neon street scene is good, but on a phone the HUD fights it and the controls hide. The only action button is a ghost ring that vanishes over the neon, there is no visible movement control, the top-right buttons are cramped and below the minimum size, and a permanent, cryptic chapter banner sits over the very skyline the walk is meant to show off. The tea terrace with customers, the whole point of this walk, is a 25px cluster of empty-looking stools next to the crosshair, while the street-level shopfront steals the light. Fix safe areas, make Use solid and context-aware, add a ghost joystick, auto-hide the banner, and light and enlarge the terrace.
